saints.name: St. Bruno
saints.title: Priest and Founder
saints.shortBlurb: A learned master of Reims who fled fame for the silence of the mountains and founded the Carthusian Order…
biography: Born at Cologne about 1030, Bruno studied at Reims and rose to head its cathedral school from 1057 to 1075, numbering among his pupils the future Pope Urban II. Made chancellor of the diocese, he opposed the violent and simoniacal Archbishop Manasses of Reims until Manasses was driven from the see in 1080.

With six companions he was settled by Hugh, Bishop of Grenoble, in the wild valley of Chartreuse in 1084, where they built an oratory and scattered cells, the first charterhouse and mother of the Carthusian Order. Called to Rome in 1090 by his former pupil Urban II, Bruno refused the archbishopric of Reggio and begged back his hermit's life.

The pope kept him in Italy, and in 1091 he founded a second charterhouse, Our Lady della Torre in Calabria, under the patronage of Count Roger of Sicily, dying there on 6 October 1101. Never formally canonized, his cult was approved by Leo X in 1514 and extended to the whole Church in 1623; his order, by the old saying, was never reformed because never deformed.

canonization.canonized: Cultus approved 1514 by Pope Leo X; feast extended to the whole Church 1623
